person.valueProp: I translate ambiguous business problems into structured analytical solutions — from ETL pipelines and dimensional data models to executive dashboards that leaders actually use to decide.

narrative: I'm a data-driven analyst and consultant who lives in the space between a vague business question and a clear, defensible answer. My job is to structure the problem, find and shape the right data, and deliver an output a decision-maker can act on with confidence.

I've done this across very different worlds — forensic investigations at EY, regional supply-chain analytics at Nestlé, machine-learning for mobile gaming at Babil Games, and custom BI for enterprise clients at Advanced Business Solutions. The common thread: converting messy, multi-source inputs into synthesized findings that hold up under scrutiny.

I care equally about the engineering (pipelines, data models, performance) and the communication (the chart, the framing, the one number that matters). The best analytics work is invisible — it just makes the right decision feel obvious.
knownFor: Structuring ambiguous problems into clear, testable analytical frameworks
End-to-end delivery: data acquisition → modeling → dashboard → adoption
Dashboards executives actually open every morning
Translating between technical detail and business context

principles.title: Decision-first

principles.title: Defensible by design

principles.body: A dashboard nobody opens is a failed project. I design for the daily user.

principles.title: Reusable foundations
principles.body: Models and pipelines built to be reused across teams, not one-off reports.

projects.title: Vendor-Managed Inventory Analytics
projects.tagline: One consolidated Power BI product replacing hours of manual data wrangling across 7 markets.
projects.context: A regional Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) team manages distributor stock cover across 7 markets — ensuring optimal replenishment by analyzing delivery schedules, demand, and sell-in / sell-out. Good decisions depend on accurate stock measures, accurate forecasts, and tight distributor engagement.
projects.problem: The team burned hours every week pulling data from multiple disconnected sources, then manually parsing, formatting, aggregating, and reconciling it before any decision could be made. The process was slow, error-prone, and inconsistent between markets.
approach: Ran structured discovery with the VMI team to capture the business nuances and the few factors that actually drive their success.
Designed a single Power BI product consolidating every data source plus the transformations needed for full stock visibility.
Ingested Distributor Stock Cover (DSC) and Sell-In/Sell-Out (SISO) via MDX over the SAP BW connector.
Automated proposal (ARS) and Inter-Market Supply (IMS) target files through an Azure Data Factory pipeline into SQL, ending broken file connections.
Built a composite-key data model (distributor × SKU × date) and offset tables to show current / +1mo / +2mo IMS targets on a single row.
Validated against the legacy system to guarantee the new numbers were accurate and complete.
projects.solution: A standardized, self-serve report giving the whole region full visibility of stock cover, SISO trends, proposal cadence, and forecast targets — segmented by distributor and proposal, with time-series views (daily, MTD, monthly) and a tabular proposal view surfacing every KPI per SKU on one record.
impact: ≈50 man-hours per week returned to the team across all 7 markets.
Extraction / parsing / formatting errors effectively eliminated.
A single standardized view shared region-wide, improving communication and consistency.
A reusable data model other teams can build on for new use cases.

challenges.title: Unclear requirements
challenges.body: Stakeholders weren't sure what they wanted, so meetings dragged. I used a tight set of guiding questions to converge on needs that were both valuable and technically feasible.

challenges.title: Complex calculations
challenges.body: IMS-target offsets and cross-table logic were hard. I worked through docs, forums, and brainstorming with domain experts to land robust solutions.

challenges.title: Unfamiliar MDX
challenges.body: I hadn't written MDX before. Studying the docs and existing statements got me to correct, performant queries.

challenges.title: Fragile cloud connections
challenges.body: Direct connections to cloud CSVs broke on every file change. Ingesting through an ADF pipeline into SQL made the connection seamless and durable.

learnings: Deep supply-chain (SCM) domain knowledge I can reuse on future projects.
A thorough, practical grasp of MDX and of designing table relationships.
Lock requirements with all parties before execution to cut rework.
How to motivate a cross-market team to carry a project over the line.
nextSteps: Ship a multi-country roll-up dedicated to the team lead for cross-market inventory analysis.
Layer forecast-accuracy tracking and anomaly flags on top of the existing model.
Promote the composite-key model into a shared semantic layer for other analytics teams.

projects.title: Player Churn & Value Modeling
projects.tagline: An XGBoost model reaching 97% accuracy, owned from problem definition to the client presentation.
projects.context: In free-to-play mobile gaming, retention is everything. Leadership needed a reliable, explainable signal for which players were likely to churn so engagement and monetization could be targeted where they mattered.
projects.problem: Raw behavioral and transactional data lived across systems with no consolidated, model-ready foundation — and no shared definition of churn the business agreed on.
approach: Defined the churn problem and success criteria with stakeholders before any modeling.
Built the data-warehouse layer and engineered behavioral / monetization features.
Trained and tuned an XGBoost classifier, reaching 97% accuracy on held-out data.
Translated model output into business framing and presented to senior management.
projects.solution: A reproducible modeling pipeline plus a clear, client-ready readout connecting model signals to concrete retention and monetization levers.
impact: Delivered a 97%-accuracy churn model the business could trust.
Gave leadership an explainable, prioritized view of at-risk players.
Established a reusable warehousing + feature foundation for future models.

challenges.title: No shared churn definition
challenges.body: Aligned stakeholders on a single, measurable definition before modeling to avoid rework.

challenges.title: Fragmented data
challenges.body: Built a consolidated warehouse layer so features were consistent and reproducible.

learnings: Explainability earns trust faster than raw accuracy with non-technical leaders.
The data foundation, not the algorithm, is usually the hard part.
nextSteps: Monitor model drift and retrain on a schedule.
Connect predictions to an automated, A/B-tested engagement workflow.

projects.solution: Custom analytics solutions and client-ready reporting frameworks with built-in data quality and access governance.

challenges.title: Shifting requirements

learnings: Governance designed in early is far cheaper than bolted on later.
nextSteps: Templatize the reporting layer for faster client onboarding.
